problems: No pyOCD release that honours the Pname attribute is named; the maintainer only said pyOCD would need to be extended
The workaround 'prefer sector erase over --chip' is not in the thread
The thread ends without a fix, so resolution 'workaround' is not supported
The maintainer doubted the bus-error explanation because the error code 0x20000201 came back from EraseChip()
cause_fixed: STM32WB is dual-core with shared flash, and its reference manual says a mass erase issued by CPU1 (the Cortex-M4) is ignored with a bus error. pyOCD always ran flash operations on the first core and ignored the Pname of the pack's algorithm element, although the maintainer noted the failure was reported by EraseChip() rather than as a bus error. A full chip erase with that pack also failed in Keil MDK.
fix_fixed: No fix in the thread; the maintainer said pyOCD would have to run the flash algorithm on the core named by the algorithm's Pname attribute.

problems: Resolution 'fixed-in-release': the thread only says PR #262 was raised
Creating the .armlm/.iarlm folders addresses a separate devcontainer build failure and was only the reporter's suggestion; maintainers were unsure about it
cause_fixed: vcpkg changed its activation command: 'vcpkg activate' no longer works and 'vcpkg-shell activate' takes its place, so the postCreate script fails.
fix_fixed: Call vcpkg-shell activate in the postCreate script (proposed in PR #262). Separately, the devcontainer build can fail when the .armlm or .iarlm folders mounted by devcontainer.json do not exist; creating them was suggested by the reporter.

problems: 'Run pyocd list to check' is not in the thread
The reporter never confirmed that placing the DLL solved it; another user still had trouble after copying the library to many places
cause_fixed: On Windows pyOCD found no libusb library, so STLink and CMSIS-DAP v2 probes were unsupported and the server kept waiting for a probe; 'pip install libusb' did not provide the DLL.
fix_fixed: Download libusb from libusb.info and place its DLL next to python.exe, matching the 32- or 64-bit architecture of the Python installation (maintainer's advice, not confirmed in the thread).

problems: Version 0.8 is not in the thread (the reporter only says 'latest pyOCD')
The VPN explanation came from a maintainer who hit it himself; the reporter ran no VPN and the original cause stayed unknown
cause_fixed: pyOCD could not bind the GDB port 3333, which points to another service holding that port (a maintainer saw this with a VPN client); for the reporter the problem later disappeared and its origin stayed unclear.
fix_fixed: Start the server on another port with -p (for example 3334); a server that then sits silently is just waiting for gdb to connect.

problems: 'Fixed in 1.5.0 era' is not in the thread, which only says 'Fixed'
cause_fixed: cbuildgen replaces spaces in the RTE path with underscores (meant for component classes such as 'CMSIS Driver') and also did so for spaces above the RTE folder, so a custom rtedir containing a space pointed to a path that does not exist.
fix_fixed: The tool was changed to replace only spaces below the RTE folder; with a version lacking the change, keep spaces out of the rtedir path.

problems: 'Otherwise the highest version wins' misstates the rule: the highest Cversion is picked only among IDs that match a single component when Cversion is ignored
The trailing '&' for an empty Cvariant was only proposed
The thread announces a change for CMSIS-Toolbox 2.0.0-dev3 (apparently isDefaultVariant handling), not the explicit-variant workaround
cause_fixed: csolution first collects the matching components and then picks one, ahead of the RTE model logic that honours isDefaultVariant, so the pack's default variant was ignored. A partly specified component resolves only to a single match (Cversion not considered), and then the highest Cversion is taken.
fix_fixed: Give the full component ID including the Cvariant so that it resolves to one match. Respecting isDefaultVariant was announced for CMSIS-Toolbox 2.0.0-dev3; a trailing & to denote an empty Cvariant was proposed.

problems: Version 0.4 is not in the thread
cause_fixed: The new W7500 target's flash algorithm definition had analyzer_supported off and a begin_data RAM address that did not work, so gdb 'load' failed.
fix_fixed: In the target's flash algorithm definition set analyzer_supported to true and begin_data to a usable RAM address (0x20002000 on the W7500).

problems: No release containing the fix is named in the thread
The advice to use 'pyocd flash' or the flash loader instead of raw writes is not in the thread
'Early 2019 builds' is not in the thread
cause_fixed: program_phrase() in pyOCD's flash code tested an undefined variable flashPtr in its alignment check instead of the address, so a W32 to a flash address raised NameError.
fix_fixed: The maintainers took the bug on; the reporter's correction is to check address % min_len in program_phrase(). Use a pyOCD version that carries the correction.

problems: The thread does not say what CMSIS-Toolbox 1.5.0 changed: an earlier plan was to apply define: and add-path: only to C/C++ sources, and duplicate removal in csolution was only asked about
cause_fixed: Defines add up through the hierarchy, so a define given both globally and for a single file appears twice on the command line, which the IAR assembler rejects.
fix_fixed: Do not repeat a global define at file level. The thread points to CMSIS-Toolbox 1.5.0 for the fix without saying which change it contains.

problems: 'CI build of June 2026' is not in the thread; it only says CI artifacts were validated
cause_fixed: For Zephyr/West projects the *.cbuild.yml file list is completed only during cbuild setup from compile_commands.json, but the Outline view was refreshed right after solution conversion.
fix_fixed: The extension now refreshes the Outline after cbuild setup for Zephyr/West projects; validated with CI artifacts, no release named.

problems: '2.8.0 normalises the short version' is not stated; the thread only says the problem was fixed in 2.8.0
Deleting the stale generated files and re-running setup is not in the thread
cause_fixed: The rejected *.cbuild.yml had been generated by CMSIS-Toolbox 2.7.0, whose problem was fixed in 2.8.0; it was not a schema defect.
fix_fixed: Update to CMSIS-Toolbox 2.8.0 or later so that the cbuild files are generated by the new version.

problems: Version 0.32 is not in the thread
cause_fixed: A copy-and-paste bug kept pyOCD from applying the requested SWD frequency to an ST-Link V3. After the fix the measured clock still differs from the request because of how the ST-Link V3 derives its frequencies, the same as in Keil MDK.
fix_fixed: Use a pyOCD with the fix, first available on the develop branch (pip install from git @develop); a new stlink.v3_prescaler option selects the probe's prescaler.

problems: Newer toolboxes reporting duplicates in csolution and a '2.5.0 duplicate-source error' are not in the thread
Versions '2.3 to 2.5' are not in the thread
cause_fixed: Two components of the pack list the same source file. cbuild2cmake compiles it for each component and the linker reports duplicate symbols, while the RteModel and cbuildgen silently dropped the duplicate and hid the problem.
fix_fixed: Treat it as a component design error in the pack and let only one selected component contribute the file, for example through a common component the others depend on; packchk is to detect such packs (devtools #1499).

problems: Versions '2.6.0' does not match the thread: the error message appears in nightly csolution 2.6.0+p56, and no affected release is named
cause_fixed: 'csolution list configs' without an input *.csolution.yml crashed silently with a non-zero exit code instead of reporting the missing argument.
fix_fixed: Pass the solution file, e.g. csolution list configs <name>.csolution.yml. Nightly builds from 2024-12-02 (csolution 2.6.0+p56) report 'input yml files were not specified' instead of crashing.

problems: Running cpackget update-index is not in the thread
'The maintainers verified a fix in a later nightly' goes beyond the single comment 'Verified'
'Fixed in a later nightly' in versions is not in the thread
cause_fixed: An old pdsc of the pack in the .Web folder was no longer being updated, so cpackget did not find the expected pdsc in the downloaded pack.
fix_fixed: Delete the outdated pdsc of that pack from .Web and add the pack again; the issue was later marked verified without naming a release.

problems: 'Released after 1.0.0' is not confirmed; the reporter was still waiting for the fix in the next build
Resolution 'fixed-in-release' is not confirmed by the thread
cause_fixed: A regression in pyOCD's hidapi backend broke CMSIS-DAP v1 probes that report no USB serial number, such as the GD-Link, although 'pyocd list' shows the probe; extension 0.5.0 still worked.
fix_fixed: Use a pyOCD build with the hidapi fix from the CMSIS Debugger team (the reporter verified a test build). To try a custom pyOCD in the extension, change its path in launch.json and in every pyocd entry of tasks.json.

problems: 'Helpers not mentioned in the main docs' is not in the thread
cause_fixed: pyocd list and pyocd pack show are built on Python helpers that a program can call directly.
fix_fixed: Use pyocd.core.helpers.ConnectHelper.get_all_connected_probes(blocking=False) to get probe objects with product_name and unique_id, and pyocd.target.pack.pack_target.ManagedPacks.get_installed_packs() for the installed packs (vendor, pack, version, pack file).

problems: The CDT GDB Adapter version was only presumed: the fix was to ship with the next release, 'presumably v2.5.0'
cause_fixed: The CDT GDB Adapter failed to decode non-UTF-8 bytes in strings read for the RTOS view and logged each failure to the Debug Console.
fix_fixed: The fix was merged into the CDT GDB Adapter for its next release (expected to be 2.5.0); use a CMSIS Debugger that ships that adapter release.

problems: 'Build with the debug profile so it never sleeps' contradicts the thread: the Mbed OS debug profile still enters sleep, only not deep sleep, so DBGMCU_CR must still be set
cause_fixed: After a power cycle the Mbed OS application starts and goes to sleep without the DBGMCU_CR debug-in-sleep bits set; pyOCD sets these bits only when it connects and cannot wake a target that is already sleeping.
fix_fixed: In debug builds keep the firmware from sleeping at all, or have it set the DBGMCU_CR bits (such as DBG_SLEEP) at startup. Connecting under reset (connect_mode=under-reset) allowed a connection, and updating the ST-Link firmware cleared the error on most of the boards.

problems: Using a CMSIS-DAP or J-Link probe instead is not in the thread
cause_fixed: ST-Link firmware V2J37S7 apparently refuses to work with non-STM32 devices (the maintainer's belief); with V2J34S7 the nRF52832 could be flashed again.
fix_fixed: Downgrade the ST-Link firmware to an older version such as V2J34S7.

problems: CMSIS Debugger 1.2.0 is not in the thread
The reporter wrote a cbuild-run.yml himself before the example-project route was suggested, so 'after doing this' misattributes the result
That the missing debug sequences made GDB lose its frames is inferred; the maintainer only said memory and core register accesses could fail
cause_fixed: The debugger ran standalone with a makefile build and no *.cbuild-run.yml, so the debug sequences of the device pack (on the STM32G474 the DBGMCU_CR setup) were missing, which can make memory and core register accesses fail; once a cbuild-run.yml was in place the GDB crash went away. The 'outside buffer bounds' error is a separate Peripheral Inspector bug.
fix_fixed: Provide a *.cbuild-run.yml. Without a CMSIS Solution build, create an example or blank solution for the board with the CMSIS Solution extension and reuse its generated *.cbuild-run.yml, *.dbgconf, launch.json and tasks.json, adjusted to your build output.

problems: The fix (close other programs, replug) is inferred; the thread was closed as old without a resolution
The example programs (an IDE, mbed tools, a serial tool) are not in the thread
cause_fixed: pyOCD's pywinusb backend timed out opening the probe and hit an assert, which the maintainers read as another process (not pyOCD, which opens the probe exclusively) holding the board.
fix_fixed: Not confirmed in the thread: find and close the other program that has the board open, then start pyocd-gdbserver again.

problems: 'Throttles those requests' is not in the thread, which only names the fix #888
Errors still appear now and then after the fix
cause_fixed: Requests that the Component Viewer sent to GDB could leave the CDT GDB Adapter or GDB unresponsive while running and stepping; Reset Target did not always recover.
fix_fixed: Update to CMSIS Debugger 1.4.1 or later, which contains the fix (#888); error messages may still appear occasionally, but run control no longer hangs as easily.

problems: The validated build is the CMSIS Solution nightly of 2026-06-09, which bundles a CMSIS-Toolbox nightly with the new launch script; 'a toolbox nightly after 2026-06-09' does not match
That TIMEOUT fails because stdin is redirected is an inference; the thread says the TIMEOUT statements probably cause the error
cause_fixed: The generator's Windows launch script contained TIMEOUT statements, which probably produce the repeated error when the extension starts the generator; the cgen.yml was still written and the application built.
fix_fixed: Use the CMSIS Solution nightly of 2026-06-09 or later, which bundles a CMSIS-Toolbox nightly with the updated generator launch script.

problems: The user-script fix was untested by the maintainer and failed for both users on pyOCD 0.21.0; no working fix is in the thread
'Needs a pyOCD newer than 0.21' and 'user scripts need >= 0.22' are not in the thread
'After a power cycle' and 'firmware that sets DBGEN' are not in the thread; it says STM32CubeIDE probably sets DBGEN while flashing
The DBGEN cause is a maintainer hypothesis, stated as fact
cause_fixed: The maintainer suspected, from the debug sequences of the STM32G0 pack, that RCC_APBENR1.DBGEN must be set to clock the debug resources before the ROM tables are read; flashing with STM32CubeIDE probably leaves it set, which would explain why the error disappears after flashing that way.
fix_fixed: Proposed, not confirmed: a pyocd_user.py whose will_init_target hook inserts a task after 'create_aps' that writes 0x08000000 to 0x4002103c. On pyOCD 0.21.0 the parameter had to be named init_sequence, and the script then still failed with a NoneType error.

problems: 'IPSR=3 means HardFault' is not in the thread
Checking the stack location is not in the thread
The reported LPC55S36 RevD1 case remained unsolved; the address fix came from another user with another chip
cause_fixed: The flash algorithm did not reach its expected halt. For one user with another chip the algorithm was loaded at 0x20000000, which is not valid memory on that MCU, so its init routine did not run correctly. For the LPC55S36 RevD1 board in the report the reporter suspected changes in the new chip ROM; that case stayed unsolved.
fix_fixed: Check that the flash algorithm is loaded into RAM that exists on the device and move its load address if not; that fixed it for the other user.

problems: The mechanism (no file watch because cbuild-idx.yml did not list the cgen file) is not in the thread
'csolution now lists the cgen file before it exists' is not in the thread
cause_fixed: The extension did not react when a generator created the missing .cgen.yml, so no solution convert followed.
fix_fixed: Use the CMSIS Solution nightly of 2026-09-09 or later; there cbuild setup runs once the generator has finished.

problems: The thread only doubts that the API works from several threads; the digest states it as fact
The suggested approach was not confirmed by the asker
cause_fixed: Each probe flashed fine on its own; a responder doubted that pyOCD's Python API can be used from several threads at once.
fix_fixed: Suggested, not confirmed: run the pyocd command line once per probe with that probe's unique ID, for example from a multiprocessing pool, instead of threads in one process.

problems: The CI advice is not in the thread; the CI side said an error should stop the test, and the maintainers then considered reporting it as a warning in pyocd run
'So they stay at error level' ignores that later turn
cause_fixed: pyOCD reads the RTT buffers continuously. On Alif E8 SWD/JTAG WAIT errors tend to occur sporadically just after the target is reset and starts running, also influenced by the processor stubs programmed with the Alif SE tools; a failed iteration is dropped and RTT processing continues.
fix_fixed: A single error after reset or a few sporadic ones are usually not critical and only lower the RTT bandwidth (SystemView data can overflow); persistent errors mean RTT no longer works and point to the target or the debug link. The maintainers planned to check whether pyocd run can report it as a warning.

problems: 'March 2024' is not in the thread
cause_fixed: Build metadata after + must be ignored for comparison (SemVer), but cpackget compared it literally against the releases in the pdsc. Packs differing only in metadata are the same version and share one install folder.
fix_fixed: Use a cpackget with PR #273 (validated in a CI build), or leave the +meta part out of the pack specification.

problems: 'Sometimes 0 bytes' is not in the thread
Checking the network or proxy is not in the thread
Deleting the file in .Download by hand is offered as an equal alternative, but the reporter says the manual removal had not helped while rm --purge did
cause_fixed: The pack file cached in .Download was damaged by a failed download, and cpackget used that cached file.
fix_fixed: Run cpackget rm --purge ARM::CMSIS@6.1.0 to drop the cached pack, then cpackget add ARM::CMSIS@6.1.0 again; if it still fails, rerun with -v to get a log.

problems: The fix (for-compiler: AC6 conditions, GCC equivalents such as retargeting sources) is not in the thread, which only diagnoses the cause
That ARM::Device:Definition exists only for Arm Compiler is not stated; the thread speaks generally of toolchain-specific modules
cause_fixed: Some components listed in the project have toolchain-specific files (for example assembler sources) and are not available for GCC, so csolution cannot resolve them after the compiler is switched; GCC itself is supported by the tools.
fix_fixed: Replace or remove the components that are only available for Arm Compiler when building with GCC.

problems: #1669 was merged into the develop branch; no release is named
'Reads memory in chunks' is an assumption about the code
cause_fixed: pyOCD's RTT control block search failed when the control block ID string crossed a 32-byte boundary.
fix_fixed: Workaround: shift the search start by 16 bytes (one of -a 0x20000000 or -a 0x20000010 works) or align the control block to 16 bytes. The fix (#1669) is merged into pyOCD's develop branch.

problems: 'CMSIS Debugger 0.2/1.0 era' is not in the thread; it names the pyOCD build v0.0.0-standalone-cbuild3
cause_fixed: The AP address classes lacked apid handling for APv2.
fix_fixed: Use a pyOCD whose AP address classes handle apid, first in the standalone build v0.0.0-standalone-cbuild3.

problems: 'Later releases' is not in the thread; only a CMSIS Debugger nightly build was tested
Declaring a memory element in the DFP as an alternative is not in the thread
cause_fixed: pyOCD 0.45.0 rejects a flash algorithm whose RAMstart lies outside every explicit RAM region of the pack description. The algorithm is dropped and the flash region ends up without a flash instance, although the address is valid RAM on the device.
fix_fixed: Use a pyOCD with pyOCD PR 2012, tested in a CMSIS Debugger nightly build, where programming the M55M1 worked again.

problems: 'Regression after 0.19' and 'merged shortly after 0.20.0' are not in the thread; it names a regression after PR #595 and a workaround in PR #616 verified on master
cause_fixed: While scanning USB devices, pyOCD's pyusb backend read the interface name strings of every device; an Android phone without a language ID made pyusb raise ValueError, which aborted the probe scan (likely a regression from PR #595).
fix_fixed: Use a pyOCD with the workaround from PR #616 (verified on master), or unplug the other device.

problems: Symptom names Flash/RA2A1_256K.FLM; the thread shows Flash/RA6M5_2M.FLM
Version 0.34 is not in the thread
The thread welcomes PR #1461 but does not confirm a release
cause_fixed: The Renesas pack stores its pdsc in a subdirectory; pyOCD found the pdsc but resolved the algorithm paths relative to the archive root.
fix_fixed: pyOCD was to be changed to accept this non-standard layout (PR #1461); use a pyOCD that includes it.

problems: 'CMSIS Debugger 0.2+' is not in the thread; it names the pyOCD build v0.0.0-standalone-cbuild4
cause_fixed: Before programming, pyOCD reads flash to compare it with the image; on an erased LPC55S69 these direct reads cause bus errors.
fix_fixed: Use a pyOCD that skips reading erased sectors when the flash algorithm provides a Verify function, first in the standalone build v0.0.0-standalone-cbuild4.

problems: 'Release after 1.5.0' and 'same fix as for the Arm-Packs:: case' are not in the thread, which only says duplicate of #805, fixed in the next release
The workarounds (omit the vendor, --no-check-schema) are not in the thread
cause_fixed: The regular expression for the component ID in the yml schema did not allow a hyphen in the vendor part; the component itself is valid.
fix_fixed: Fixed in the next tools release (duplicate of devtools #805); update the tools.

problems: Group-level add-paths does not fix the reported error: it only applies to the group's own sources, while the header was needed by a component (the reporter's group-level attempt failed)
The cause leaves out that add-paths only affects the sources at its own level
cause_fixed: add-paths is accepted for a single file, a group, a component, the project, a layer, the solution and build or target types, but not for the files list, and it only affects the sources compiled at that level, so a path given for a group does not reach a component's sources. Repeating the add-paths key in one map is invalid YAML because keys must be unique.
fix_fixed: Put the include path where the failing source is compiled: on the component that needs it (e.g. Device:STM32Cube HAL:Common) or at project level, and write several paths as one list (add-paths: [., ./targets/board] or one entry per line).

problems: Giving the control block address explicitly is not in the thread
cause_fixed: pyOCD handled the pname of a single-core target wrongly, so the lookup of the RTT control block by its ELF symbol failed.
fix_fixed: Update to pyOCD 0.43.1 / CMSIS Debugger 1.4.1 or later, which contain pyOCD PR #1923.

problems: 'Fixed in April 2024' is not in the thread
Installing the dependency packs explicitly first is not in the thread
cause_fixed: Regression in cpackget 2.1.1: for dependencies of the form >=x.y.z cpackget uses an internal open upper bound (x.y.z:_) that the range comparison did not support, and the version and range arguments were swapped in the modifier resolution.
fix_fixed: Use a cpackget newer than 2.1.1 that contains both corrections; version 2.0.1 still installed the requirements correctly.

problems: The specification regex was only proposed for correction in a PR (Open-CMSIS-Pack-Spec #123); the thread does not confirm it was merged
cause_fixed: The semantic-version expression taken from the pack index specification had a repeating capture group that returned a variable number of matches for dotted pre-release parts, which broke version splitting.
fix_fixed: Use a cpackget release after 0.4.1 with the merged bugfix; a matching correction of the specification's regex was proposed.

problems: Affected versions '2.2.x' are not in the thread
The thread does not say the final fix drops -mfpu and uses sysroot; that was the attached workaround, and the final fix also had to keep the compilation database complete
Only 2.3.0-dev0 was confirmed, not the 2.3.0 release
cause_fixed: The CLANG toolchain file used an -mfpu option that crashes the compiler, a wrong CLANG_ARCH runtime folder, and explicit -isystem paths that did not find the standard headers.
fix_fixed: Use CMSIS-Toolbox 2.3.0-dev0 or later, confirmed to work with LLVM 17. Before that, the workaround was a CLANG cmake file without -mfpu that uses a sysroot option instead of the -isystem paths.

problems: Choosing the reset type via load-setup post-reset in the solution is not in the thread
Versions 'pyOCD 0.44 and 0.45' are not in the thread
cause_fixed: The default post-load reset for cbuild-run targets is a hardware reset. With the default ResetHardware sequence the debug connection can be lost right after it, the board uninit steps then fail, and load exits non-zero although programming worked; the CMSIS Load pre-launch task then shows an error pop-up.
fix_fixed: Use a pyOCD with PR 1971: a hardware post-load reset runs after board uninit, and for other reset types failures are reported as information with exit code 0 when flashing succeeded.

problems: 'Or give it with --config' is not in the thread
Versions '0.19 to 0.20' are not in the thread
cause_fixed: The target override and test_binary options were placed in a file called test_boards.yaml. pyOCD reads its config from pyocd.yaml (the functional tests switched to that name), so the target stayed at the generic cortex_m type, which has no flash support or memory map.
fix_fixed: Rename the file to pyocd.yaml and set target_override and test_binary there (or pass --target), then check the 'Target type is ...' log line to confirm the target.

problems: Resolution 'fixed-in-release': the thread ends with PRs created (CMSIS_6 #260, Cortex_DFP #22), not merged or released
cause_fixed: The linker symbol __StackSeal is 64 bit but was declared as uint32_t in the startup template.
fix_fixed: Declare __STACK_SEAL as extern uint64_t in the startup file; the reporter opened PRs for the CMSIS_6 template (#260) and for Cortex_DFP (#22).
